notification.send.destination: Use a configured destination alias from registeredResources.items[].value, not a channel ID or webhook URL. Only registered, enabled and configured destinations can execute, including under broad grants. The signed Workflow endpoint remains a private resource attribute and is never an action input.
notification.send.formats: contentFormat is explicit: simple accepts nonempty text and optional nonempty title only and creates an Adaptive Card 1.2 envelope; microsoft accepts a full Adaptive Card message envelope or MessageCard. Microsoft objects retain native extension values after structural validation.
notification.send.microsoft: An Adaptive envelope uses type message and nonempty attachments; each attachment needs contentType application/vnd.microsoft.card.adaptive and a card with type AdaptiveCard, a numeric dotted version string, and body array of objects. A MessageCard uses @type MessageCard, @context http://schema.org/extensions or its HTTPS form, and at least one nonempty summary or text string; every supplied summary and text must be nonempty. Supply exactly one of type or @type; a competing key is refused even when null. Microsoft extension values remain unchanged.
notification.send.limits: Full action inputs and serialized outgoing JSON each have a 24 KiB limit and depth 32, also respecting a smaller configured HTTP body limit. Oversized content is refused rather than truncated.
notification.send.delivery: A successful receipt confirms Workflow endpoint acceptance, not Workflow completion or a visible Teams message. The provider does not automatically retry. Inspect uncertain outcomes before another send; saving an acceptance response locally does not change delivery or retry safety.
notification.send.validation: Only type and @type have fixed values in the content schema: message and MessageCard. A denial may explain those constants before a format or conflict rule. With simple, omit both keys. With microsoft, keep the chosen discriminator and omit the competing key, including a null key; changing its value does not resolve the conflict.
